title: Programmes for Schools to Identify and Support Students with Adverse Childhood Experiences
what_it_is: Programmes for Schools to Identify and Support Students with Adverse Childhood Experiences

sections.label: School support for abused students
sections.summary: Educators are trained to spot abuse signs, refer distressed students to counsellors and welfare officers, report cases to authorities, and work with community partners.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Across our preschools and schools, educators are trained to look out for signs of physical, behavioural or emotional changes in our students and recognise signs of child abuse.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Students in distress are referred to school counsellors and our student welfare officers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Such cases are also reported to the authorities, such as the Early Childhood Development Agency and the Child Protective Service for investigation and intervention.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Our schools also work closely with community partners, such as the REACH, or the Response, Early Intervention and Assessment in Community Mental Health, teams so that affected students receive the necessary specialised assistance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: We will continue to help these students develop safe and positive relationships in our schools so that the impact of their adverse experiences is reduced.
